k.q: Calculate combined uncompressed file sizes using an array and running total.
k.code:
array fileMB = [3,5,2]
totalMB = 0
for i = 0 to 2
    totalMB = totalMB + fileMB[i]
next i
print(totalMB)
p: Trace the running total and predict the output in MB.
Change fileMB[1] to 8; predict the new total.
Convert the changed total to KB using 1 MB = 1,000 KB.
k.a: Totals for 3,5,2 MB: 3 → 8 → 10 MB, so output is 10. Changing the second file to 8 gives 3 → 11 → 13 MB. This is 13,000 KB using decimal storage units; file-system overhead is ignored.

e: Give the output of summing [4,1,3]. [2 marks]
Explain why index 4 is invalid for a four-element zero-indexed array. [2 marks]
Valid indexes are 0,1,2,3; index 4 is out of bounds.
Explain how to count even values in an array. [3 marks]
Iterate each element; if value MOD 2 = 0 then increment counter; output counter.

x: A three-element zero-indexed array has last index 3.
r: State two CPU factors affecting performance.
Clock speed, cache size, number of cores (any two).
Explain why meaningful variable names aid maintainability.
They make purpose easier to understand and reduce debugging/maintenance effort.
Differentiate a function and a procedure.
A function returns a value; a procedure performs an action and does not need to return a value.
Explain the role of the Control Unit.
Coordinates CPU operations and controls execution of instructions.

stretch.task: Extend the same file-size loop to count how many files are at least 5 MB while still calculating total storage.
stretch.hint: Keep totalMB and add fileCount; increment fileCount only when fileMB[i] >= 5.
stretch.answer: For files [3,5,2], total=10 MB and count=1. At threshold 5, the 5 MB file is included.

mastery.task: For [42,78,78,61,35], write one algorithm that finds the highest mark and counts how many times it occurs. Test tied highs and all-equal values.
mastery.hint: Initialise highest from the first element; reset tie count on a new high and increment it on equality.
mastery.answer: A valid one-pass solution: highest=first; ties=1; for every later item if value>highest then highest=value,ties=1 else if value==highest then ties++. Example: highest78 occurs twice; all equal returns the list length.
